messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the RFC — proposing we split the sidecar responsibilities into two surfaces: Domain-sidecars (tenant-specific business logic like routing, personalization hooks) and Infra-sidecars (observability, batching, KV caching, cross-tenant optimizations). Goal is clearer ownership + ability for infra to iterate on hot-path optimizations without touching domain code.

sam: +1. High level looks good. Can you bullet the migration approach? main concerns: data ownership, rollout safety, and added latency on hot path.

maria: Short migration plan: 
1) Define a stable gRPC facade (SidecarFacade v1) that domain services call.
2) Implement Infra-sidecar behind a feature-flag that the facade proxies to.
3) Move non-critical work (telemetry export, async enrichments) to infra-sidecar first.
4) Run per-tenant canaries, collect p95/p99; rollback via flag.
5) Iteratively move read-only caches, then consider full session KV handoff after perf validation.

lee: Agree with the facade approach. Suggest we keep a transparent proxy mode for at least 6 months so domain sees identical API. Example proto we can start with:
```
service SidecarFacade {
  rpc EmitTelemetry(Event) returns (Ack);
  rpc ReadSession(SessionKey) returns (Session);
  rpc WriteSession(Session) returns (Ack);
}
```
We keep v1 semantics and have the facade forward to old sidecar or infra-sidecar based on flag.

priya: Two immediate questions: 1) session KV currently lives in the sidecar — who owns migration & schema changes? 2) what's our latency guard for hot-path ops (ReadSession) so we don't regress production SLOs?

maria: Good questions. Proposal: runtime team retains write ownership for session KV initially; infra-sidecar can host read-only replicas/caches to accelerate reads. Ownership transfer only after we confirm p99 latency stays within guardrails. Latency guard: if p95 ReadSession increases by >5ms or p99 increases by >15ms during canary, we pause rollout.

sam: How will we handle batching and backpressure — risk of head-of-line blocking if infra-sidecar batches telemetry or aggregates?

lee: Implement adaptive batching with low-latency flush thresholds and sequence numbers to avoid reordering. Small example:
```
if queue.size > BATCH_THRESH: flush()
else schedule_flush(50ms)
```
Also keep an option to bypass batching for sync ReadSession calls.

infra-bot: deploy.canary started: infra-sidecar v0.3 -> staging tenant staging-42 (trace: https://ci/redwood/1234)

priya: Can we add a migration checklist doc? I can co-own with @lee. Checklist should include: proto compat tests, perf harness, cross-tenant metrics, rollback playbook, and DB migration plan (if any).

maria: Perfect — action items: priya+lee own migration doc (due EOD Fri), sam run perf spike tests against staging and measure p50/p95/p99 for ReadSession and WriteSession, i'll create the feature flag and schedule the first canary. We'll reconvene Tue 10am to review metrics.

ops-bot: Reminder: calendar invite created for Tue 10:00am; meeting ID and dial-in in the invite.

sam: ack

lee: ack, will start proto skeleton today

priya: ack :thumbsup: happy to write the checklist

maria: thanks all — major win if we can reduce churn between infra and domain teams while keeping latency intact.
